summary: Plasma-Enhanced Atomic Layer Deposition (PEALD) of ruthenium thin films was performed using bis(ethylcyclopentadienyl)ruthenium (Ru(EtCp)2) and NH3 plasma. The PEALD technique avoids the formation of interfacial metal oxide, resulting in smoother, denser films with low resistivity. The films showed excellent step coverage and were used as an adhesion layer for copper.
evidence: Plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition ~PEALD! of ruthenium thin ﬁlms was performed using an alternate supply of bis~ethylcyclopentadienyl!ruthenium @Ru(EtCp) 2# and NH 3 plasma. ... Ruthenium ﬁlms deposited by PEALD were smoother and denser in comparison with conventional ALD ﬁlm, and showed excellent step coverage. Therefore, PEALD is a useful tool for forming ruthenium thin ﬁlms for use as an adhesion layer.
